where: Section 1, first bullet under the shrink fit
problem: The direction of the outer tube's movement is reversed. When the outer tube is shrunk on, its bore opens out (its radius grows) to sit on the inner tube; it does not close in. Only the inner tube's outside is squeezed down. As written, a student would think both tubes shrink, which contradicts the physics of the fit and the sign of the residual stresses given just below.
fix: Fix the shrinkage allowance and find ps from it: the outer tube's bore opens out and the inner tube's outside is squeezed down, and these two radial deflections together equal the allowance.

where: Section 2, the 'where' note after the superposition formula
problem: 'the two hoop stresses simply add because they act on the same element in the same direction' reads as if the stresses can never cancel. They add algebraically, and a negative residual value is what reduces the tensile pressure value.
fix: the two hoop stresses are added algebraically at the same point, using the same sign convention, so a compressive (negative) residual reduces a tensile (positive) pressure stress.

problem: 'σθ is the hoop stress at radius r in metres, in N/m² (Pa)' attaches the metres to the stress instead of to r, which is confusing.
fix: σθ is the hoop stress at radius r, in N/m² (Pa); r is the radius in metres.
